items.text:
Why is Bacon's Essays still read today?

Bacon's Essays by Francis Bacon

Why is Bacon's Essays still read today?

It is the wisdom of crocodiles, that shed tears when they would devour

Certainly it is heaven upon earth, to have a man’s mind move in charity, rest in providence, and turn upon the poles of truth

But nobler spirits may converse, even in the midst of pleasures, if the mind be well guarded with constancy and resolution

In this fable he explains the common but erroneous supposition that knowledge and the conformity of the will, knowing and acting, are convertible terms

Italy was then the country in which human knowledge in all its branches was most successfully cultivated

The difficulties in princes’ business are many and great; but the greatest difficulty is often in their own mind

Children sweeten labors, but they make misfortunes more bitter; they increase the cares of life, but they mitigate the remembrance of death

His life was said to have been profligate, and his death superstitious

items.title: Plato had a warning for you.
items.text:
Plato had a warning for you.

Phaedrus by Plato

Plato had a warning for you.

PHAEDRUS: You shall hear, if you can spare time to accompany me

Whatever my advice may be worth, I should have told him to arrive at the truth first, and then come to me

Superior knowledge enables us to deceive another by the help of resemblances, and to escape from such a deception when employed against ourselves

We see therefore that even in rhetoric an element of truth is required

Is not pleading 'an art of speaking unconnected with the truth'?

The character of Greek literature sank lower as time went on

The human race may not be always ground down by bodily toil, but may have greater leisure for the improvement of the mind

And men in general recall only with difficulty the things of another world, but the mind of the philosopher has a better remembrance of them

items.title: This Studies in Pessimism line is uncomfortable.
items.text:
This Studies in Pessimism line is uncomfortable.

Studies in Pessimism by Arthur Schopenhauer

This Studies in Pessimism line is uncomfortable.

A man may call to mind the face of his friend, but not his own

Yes, but you raise transcendental questions, and you expect me to answer them in language that is only made for immanent knowledge

The inmost kernel of Christianity is the truth that suffering--_the Cross_--is the real end and object of life

What do you mean by transcendental questions and immanent knowledge?

Immanent knowledge, on the other hand, is knowledge which confines itself entirely with those bounds; so that it cannot apply to anything but actual phenomena

The answer is contradictory, I admit; but it is so simply because your life is in time, and the immortal part of you in eternity

You see what happens by trying to bring the transcendental within the limits of immanent knowledge

They ought to mind home--and be well fed and clothed--but not mixed in society

items.text:
Nobody warns you about Analects.

The Analects by Confucius

Nobody warns you about Analects.

How can a man conceal his character?' CHAP

Confucius said, 'Those who are born with the possession of knowledge are the highest class of men

Tsze-ch'in asked Tsze-kung, saying, 'When our master comes to any country, he does not fail to learn all about its government

As to those who are dull and stupid and yet do not learn;-- they are the lowest of the people.' CHAP

The superior man is anxious lest he should not get truth; he is not anxious lest poverty should come upon him.' CHAP

The Master said, 'It is by the Odes that the mind is aroused

The Master said, 'I can find no flaw in the character of Yu

He enlarged my mind with learning, and taught me the restraints of propriety

items.title: Nobody warns you about Tao Te Ching.
items.text:
Nobody warns you about Tao Te Ching.

Tao Te Ching by Lao Tzu

Nobody warns you about Tao Te Ching.

Music and dainties will make the passing guest stop (for a time)

The sage has in the world an appearance of indecision, and keeps his mind in a state of indifference to all

The great Tao (or way) is very level and easy; but people love the by-ways

In loving the people and ruling the state, cannot he proceed without any (purpose of) action?

Therefore a wise prince, marching the whole day, does not go far from his baggage waggons

If we could renounce our benevolence and discard our righteousness, the people would again become filial and kindly

If this transformation became to me an object of desire, I would express the desire by the nameless simplicity

The work is done, but how no one can see; 'Tis this that makes the power not cease to be

items.title: You have Art of War backwards.
items.text:
You have Art of War backwards.

The Art of War by Sun Tzu

You have Art of War backwards.

By means of these seven considerations I can forecast victory or defeat

Our own flags should be substituted for those of the enemy, and the chariots mingled and used in conjunction with ours

By discovering the enemy’s dispositions and remaining invisible ourselves, we can keep our forces concentrated, while the enemy’s must be divided

This is simply bringing anarchy into the army, and flinging victory away

Therefore the clever combatant imposes his will on the enemy, but does not allow the enemy’s will to be imposed on him

These are the four useful branches of military knowledge [Those, namely, concerned with (1) mountains, (2) rivers, (3) marshes, and (4) plains

The enemy’s spies who have come to spy on us must be sought out, tempted with bribes, led away and comfortably housed

To secure ourselves against defeat lies in our own hands, but the opportunity of defeating the enemy is provided by the enemy himself

Source: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/132

items.title: Why does Meditations still matter?
items.text:
Why does Meditations still matter?

Meditations by Marcus Aurelius

Why does Meditations still matter?

Nature's marvellous power of recreating out of Corruption is surely not confined to bodily things

If reason is general, then is that reason also, which prescribeth what is to be done and what not, common unto all

The motion of the mind is not as the motion of a dart

Either with Epicurus, we must fondly imagine the atoms to be the cause of all things, or we must needs grant a nature

He is a true fugitive, that flies from reason, by which men are sociable

Is my reason, and understanding sufficient for this, or no?

But for a man to grieve that by death he shall be deprived of any of these things, is both against God and reason

To a thoughtful mind such a religion as that of Rome would give small satisfaction

Source: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2680

Nobody warns you about Acres of Diamonds.

items.title: Why does Thus Spake Zarathustra still matter?
items.text:
Why does Thus Spake Zarathustra still matter?

Thus Spake Zarathustra by Friedrich Nietzsche

Why does Thus Spake Zarathustra still matter?

Never yet did truth cling to the arm of an absolute one

Let your bestowing love and your knowledge be devoted to be the meaning of the earth!

And why should not Zarathustra also learn from the people, when the people learn from Zarathustra?

Their stiff wise men: I call them wise, not stiff—thus did I learn to slur over words

Every one being allowed to learn to read, ruineth in the long run not only writing but also thinking

I wish them neither to learn afresh, nor teach anew, but only to bid farewell to their own bodies,—and thus be dumb

And verily, although a man should gain the whole world, and yet not learn one thing, ruminating, what would it profit him!

Now do they learn to laugh at themselves: do I hear rightly?

Source: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1998

items.title: Read this before you open Self-Reliance.
items.text:
Read this before you open Self-Reliance.

Self-Reliance (Essays) by Ralph Waldo Emerson

Read this before you open Self-Reliance.

Wisdom will never let us stand with any man or men on an unfriendly footing

So it fares with the wise Shakspeare and his book of life

It loses your time and blurs the impression of your character

There are all degrees of proficiency in knowledge of the world

Do we fear lest we should outsee nature and God, and drink truth dry?

All things shall be added unto it,--power, pleasure, knowledge, beauty

Character, reality, reminds you of nothing else; it takes place of the whole creation

The cheat, the defaulter, the gambler, cannot extort the knowledge of material and moral nature which his honest care and pains yield to the operative
